## CONTEXT

This research is exploratory and observational. 


### Objective
The aim of this research is to characterize carabid beetle and spider communities in vineyard agroecosystems and adjacent SNH in the Okanagan Valley. Specifically, this study explores how carabid beetle and spider diversity and community composition vary between vineyard and SNH, and if functional traits explain any of the variation.

## SPIDERS

### Data import and pre-processing

Let's import the raw spider data and summarize by site/ habitat/ year. We will filter out field margin samples from the main analysis as they were not sampled in 2025. September samples were excluded due to low trap recovery. 

Let's also calculate the total number of spiders collected, and the number of different families. Note that spiders that could not be identified to family level, either due to damage or being juveniles, are included in total spider count but not in family richness count.

```{r}
# Load spider data
spider_habitat_df <- read.csv(here::here("00_data","spider_habitat_df.csv"))

# Filter out field margins and september data from the main analysis
spider_habitat_df <- spider_habitat_df %>%
  filter(
    subhabitat != "FM",
    sample_period != "SEP"
  )

# Identify family columns from descriptor columns
family_cols <- setdiff(names(spider_habitat_df), c("pitfall_ID", "year", "habitat", "subhabitat", "family_richness", "sample_period", "site_ID", "year_established", "total_count"))

# ensure family cols are integer counts
spider_habitat_df <- spider_habitat_df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(family_cols), ~ as.integer(tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L))))

# Then re-define unid and identified categories
unid_cols <- union("UNID.", "LYCOSIDAE..juvenile.")  # add the juvenile manually
family_columns <- setdiff(family_cols, unid_cols)

# Summarize spider abundance by site_ID, habitat, sample period and year
spider_habitat_summary <- spider_habitat_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, sample_period, year) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(family_cols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    trap_count = n(),     # destroyed traps already removed earlier
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total number of spiders found in vineyards across all sites and years (including juveniles/ UNID)
total_spiders <- sum(spider_habitat_df$total_count, na.rm = TRUE)

# total number of traps
total_traps <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  summarise(total_traps = sum(trap_count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(total_traps)

# Convert wide data (family columns) into long format
spider_long_habitat <- spider_habitat_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(family_columns), names_to = "spider_family", values_to = "count") %>%
  drop_na(count) %>%  # Remove missing values
  filter(count >= 0)  # Ensure only observed families are counted

# Get a list of all families observed at least once
observed_families_habitat <- spider_long_habitat %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% 
  distinct(spider_family) %>%
  arrange(spider_family)

# View the result
print(observed_families_habitat)

# calculate relative abundance of each spider family
spider_family_rel <- spider_long_habitat %>%
  group_by(spider_family) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_abund = n / sum(n)) %>%   # relative abundance within each habitat
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(n > 0)

spider_family_rel

# calculate sample size
habitat_n <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

habitat_n

# sample size by year
habitat_n_year <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  group_by(year, habitat) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

habitat_n_year

cat("Total spiders in all habitats across all sites and years:", total_spiders, "\n")

cat(
  "Total number of observed families in all habitats across all sites and years:",
  nrow(observed_families_habitat),
  "\n"
)


cat("Total traps in all habitats across all sites and years:", total_traps, "\n")

cat("Number of site × habitat × year combinations:", nrow(spider_habitat_summary), "\n")

```

### Summary table
```{r}
# table summarizing spider family abundance by habitat/ year
spider_family_table <- spider_long_habitat %>%
  group_by(spider_family, habitat, year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_abundance = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  unite(habitat_year, habitat, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = habitat_year,
    values_from = total_abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total))

# make labels little letters for clarity
spider_family_table <- spider_family_table %>%
  mutate(spider_family = stringr::str_to_title(spider_family))

spider_family_table

# save as table
write.csv(
  spider_family_table,
  here::here("02_tables", "spider_family_table.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```


### Sample Coverage and Hill Diversity
Let's use iNEXT to evaluate sampling completeness (sample coverage) and calculate hill diversity (richness, shannon and simpson). 
Use only adult family counts (not juveniles and unidentified species)

```{r}
custom_colors <- c("VY"="#8E44AD","SNH"="#009E73")

#  Summarize by habitat
spider_by_habitat <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(family_columns), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Build iNEXT list: named abundance vectors (one per habitat)
spider_list_habitat <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(spider_by_habitat)), function(i) {
    v <- unlist(spider_by_habitat[i, family_columns], use.names = TRUE)
    v[is.na(v)] <- 0
    v
  }),
  spider_by_habitat$habitat
)

# Sample coverage + totals
spider_coverage <- DataInfo(spider_list_habitat, datatype = "abundance")

spider_coverage


# Hill numbers
spider_hill <- iNEXT(spider_list_habitat, q = c(0, 1, 2), datatype = "abundance")

spider_hill_diversity<- spider_hill$AsyEst

spider_hill_diversity


# save as csv
write.csv(
  spider_hill_diversity,
  here::here("02_tables", "spider_hill_diversity.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)


```
Sample completeness very high for both VY and SNH (>0.99). Likely so high because we are evaluating at the family level (coarse taxonomic resolution), only a few singletons/ doubletons in each habitat.

Higher observed and estimated richness in SNH (22) compared to VY (16). Pretty high confidence for both
Also higher shannon and simpson diversity in SNH's. indicates more evenness in SNH's compared to VY's.


Let's make some curves for the sample coverage and hill diversity metrics

```{r}
# Coverage-based curves
spider_sample_coverage <- ggiNEXT(spider_hill, type = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = 10)
  )

spider_sample_coverage

# sample size based Hill curves
spider_hill_size <- ggiNEXT(spider_hill, type = 1,
  facet.var = "Order.q") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of individuals",
    y = "Family diversity"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )



spider_hill_size

# Coverage-based Hill curves
spider_hill_coverage <- ggiNEXT(spider_hill, type = 3,
  facet.var="Order.q") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Sample coverage",
    y = "Family diversity"
  )

spider_hill_coverage


```



### Data Exploration
This section explores spiders by habitat type

#### Relative abundance plots
This section uses a bubble plot to visualize spider family relative abundance by habitat type

```{r}
custom_colors <- c("VY"="#8E44AD","SNH"="#009E73")

# 1) Summarise total individuals per habitat x family
spider_family_habitat_rel <- spider_long_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, spider_family) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  mutate(rel_abund = n / sum(n)) %>%   # relative abundance within each habitat
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(n > 0)


# make labels little letters for clarity
spider_family_habitat_rel <- spider_family_habitat_rel %>%
  mutate(spider_family = stringr::str_to_title(spider_family))

# 2) Order families (overall abundance across all habitats)
family_order <- spider_family_habitat_rel %>%
  group_by(spider_family) %>%
  summarise(total_n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(total_n) %>%
  pull(spider_family)

spider_family_habitat_rel <- spider_family_habitat_rel %>%
  mutate(spider_family = factor(spider_family, levels = family_order))


# 3) Bubble plot of relative abundance of each family by habitat type
spider_relative_abundance <- ggplot(spider_family_habitat_rel,
       aes(x = spider_family, y = habitat,
           size = rel_abund, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, color = "black", alpha = 1) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Relative abundance") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Habitat") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none")


spider_relative_abundance


```

#### Abundance and richness by habitat

This section uses boxplots to look at the mean abundance per trap and rarefied richness

```{r}
# define custom colors
custom_colors <- c("VY"="#8E44AD","SNH"="#009E73")

# -----------------------------
# HABITAT ABUNDACE, family RICHNESS, MEAN PER TRAP AND RAREFIED RICHNESS
# -----------------------------
# ALL HABITATS RICHNESS
fam_mat            <- as.matrix(dplyr::select(spider_habitat_summary, all_of(family_columns)))
total_abundance   <- rowSums(fam_mat)
family_richness  <- rowSums(fam_mat > 0)

#   Use the minimum total individuals among groups with > min_m_individuals
min_m_individuals <- 20L
m_candidates      <- total_abundance[total_abundance > min_m_individuals]

rarefaction_m <- if (length(m_candidates)) min(m_candidates) else NA_integer_

# Rarefy (individual-based); NA if m not available
rarefied_richness <- if (is.na(rarefaction_m)) {
  rep(NA_real_, nrow(fam_mat))
} else {
  vegan::rarefy(fam_mat, sample = rarefaction_m)
}

# Assemble final summary table
spider_habitat_data <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(site_ID, habitat, sample_period, year, trap_count) %>%
  mutate(
    total_abundance   = total_abundance,
    mean_per_trap     = ifelse(trap_count > 0, total_abundance / trap_count, NA_real_),
    family_richness  = family_richness,
    rarefied_richness = rarefied_richness,
    rarefaction_m     = rarefaction_m
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_ID, year, sample_period, habitat)

# calculate mean per trap by habitat
spider_mean_by_habitat <- spider_habitat_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(habitat) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_per_trap = mean(mean_per_trap, na.rm = TRUE),
    n             = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
spider_mean_by_habitat

# plot mean abundance per trap by Habitat (VY/ SNH)
# lets use line plots to account for paired design (each site has a VY and SNH)
# we're using mean per plot instead of total abundance to account for traps lost in the field
spider_abundance_line <- ggplot(
  spider_habitat_data,
  aes(
    x = habitat,
    y = mean_per_trap,
    group = interaction(site_ID, year)
  )
) +
  # paired lines in grey
  geom_line(
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # points coloured by habitat
  geom_point(
    aes(color = habitat),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Spider abundance",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean abundance per trap"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) + theme(
  axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16)
)


spider_abundance_line

# plots mean per trap by Habitat (VY/ SNH)
spider_mean_abundance <- ggplot(spider_habitat_data, aes(x = habitat, y = mean_per_trap, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.3, alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "black")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 75)) +
  labs(
    x = "Habitat type",
    y = "Abundance per trap"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

spider_mean_abundance

# plot rarefied richness
spider_rarefied_richness <-ggplot(spider_habitat_data, aes(x = habitat, y = rarefied_richness, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "black") +
  geom_text(
    data = habitat_n,
    aes(
      x = habitat,
      y = max(spider_habitat_data$rarefied_richness, na.rm = TRUE) + 2,
      label = paste0("n = ", n)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Spider Rarefied Richness by Habitat Type",
    x = "Habitat Type",
    y = "Spider Rarefied Richness"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

spider_rarefied_richness

```

Vineyards generally have higher mean abundance, but a little lower (rarefied) richness

#### Spider traits by habitat
This section explores uses barplots and pie charts to explore spider traits/ guilds by habitat type.

```{r}
# upload the spider traits data
spider_traits <- read.csv(here::here ("00_data", "spider_family_traits.csv"))

# join to spider habitat data (in long format)
spider_long_traits_habitat <- spider_long_habitat %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(spider_traits, spider_family, guild_code),
    by = "spider_family"
  )

# summarize guild abundance by site_ID, habitat and year
guild_abundance_habitat <- spider_long_traits_habitat %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, year, guild_code) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(count), .groups = "drop")

# pivot to wide format
guild_abundance_wide <- guild_abundance_habitat %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = guild_code,
    values_from = total_abundance,
    values_fill = 0  # fill missing combinations with 0
  )

# Make sure guild_abundance_habitat is prepared
guild_abundance_plot <- guild_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, guild_code) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop")
guild_abundance_plot <- guild_abundance_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(guild_code))


# Custom colors (edit to match your desired palette)
guild_colors <- c(
  "AMH" = "#E69F00",     # orange
  "GRH" = "#009E73",     # bluish green
  "ORW" = "#56B4E9",     # sky blue
  "SHW" = "#0072B2",     # blue
  "SPW" = "#D55E00",     # vermillion
  "SPE" = "#CC79A7",     # reddish purple
  "OTH" = "#999999",     # grey
  "SHW/ GRH" = "#F0E442", # yellow
  "SHW/ OTH" = "#7D3C98"  # black
)

guild_labels <- c(
  "AMH" = "Ambush hunters",
  "GRH" = "Ground hunters",
  "ORW" = "Orb web weavers",
  "SHW" = "Sheet web weavers",
  "SPW" = "Space web weavers",
  "SPE" = "Specialists",
  "OTH" = "Other hunters",
  "SHW/ GRH" = "Sheet web weavers/Ground hunters",
  "SHW/ OTH" = "Sheet web weavers/Other hunters"
)


# Create the stacked bar chart
ggplot(guild_abundance_plot, aes(x = habitat, y = total_abundance, fill = guild_code)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_colors, labels = guild_labels) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "No. spiders",
    fill = "Guild",
    title = "Guild composition by habitat type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# Summarize total abundance by habitat and guild, then calculate proportion
guild_prop_habitat <- guild_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, guild_code) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_abundance / sum(total_abundance))

guild_prop_habitat <- guild_prop_habitat %>%
  filter(!is.na(guild_code))

# set factor order for consistent pie layout
guild_prop_habitat$guild_code <- factor(guild_prop_habitat$guild_code)


# Plot pie chart by habitat using facet
spider_traits_pie <- ggplot(guild_prop_habitat, aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = guild_code)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar("y") +
  facet_wrap(~habitat) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_colors, labels = guild_labels) +
  labs(
    fill = "Guild",
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

spider_traits_pie 

```

No obvious difference between SNH and VY as far as traits go. Both have large proportions of specialists (mainly Zodariidae) and ground hunters (mainly Lycosidae)

## CARABIDS

### Data import and pre-processing
This section loads the carabid raw data and prepares it for modelling. 


```{r}
# Load data and coordinates for sites
carabid_habitat_df <- read.csv(here::here("00_data","carabid_habitat_df.csv"))

# Filter out field margins and september data from the main analysis
carabid_habitat_df <- carabid_habitat_df %>%
  filter(
    subhabitat != "FM",
    sample_period != "SEP"
  )


# Identify species columns
non_species <- c(
  "pitfall_ID","total_abundance","carabid_abundance","species_richness","destroyed",
  "site_code","site_ID","habitat","subhabitat","management_type",
  "sample_period","year","trap_number", "trap_count"
)

species_cols <- setdiff(names(carabid_habitat_df), non_species)

# drop any UNID (do not include in species count, only in total abundance)
unid_cols <- species_cols[grepl("^UNID\\b|^UNID\\.", species_cols)]
species_columns <- setdiff(species_cols, unid_cols)

# ensure species cols are integer counts
carabid_habitat_df <- carabid_habitat_df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(species_columns), ~ as.integer(tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L))))

# Summarize carabid abundance by site_ID, habitat, sample period and year
carabid_habitat_summary <- carabid_habitat_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, sample_period, year) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(species_columns), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    trap_count = n(),     # destroyed traps already removed earlier
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total number of carabids found in vineyards across all sites and years
total_carabids_habitat <- sum(carabid_habitat_df$total_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)

# Convert wide data (species columns) into long format
carabid_long_habitat <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(species_columns), names_to = "carabid_species", values_to = "count") %>%
  drop_na(count) %>%  # Remove missing values
  filter(count >= 0)  # Ensure only observed families are counted

# Get a list of all species observed at least once
observed_species_habitat <- carabid_long_habitat %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% 
  distinct(carabid_species) %>%
  arrange(carabid_species)


print(observed_species_habitat)


# Also group at genus level
carabid_long_genus_habitat <- carabid_long_habitat %>%
  mutate(carabid_genus = str_extract(carabid_species, "^[A-Za-z]+")) %>%  # extract genus from species name
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, carabid_genus) %>%
  summarise(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Get a list of all genera observed at least once
observed_genus_habitat <- carabid_long_genus_habitat %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% 
  distinct(carabid_genus) %>%
  arrange(carabid_genus)


print(observed_genus_habitat)

# calculate relative abundance of each spider family
carabid_genus_rel <- carabid_long_genus_habitat %>%
  group_by(carabid_genus) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_abund = n / sum(n)) %>%   # relative abundance within each habitat
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(n > 0)

carabid_genus_rel

cat("Total carabids in all habitats across all sites and years:", total_carabids_habitat, "\n")

cat(
  "Total number of observed species in all habitats across all sites and years:",
  nrow(observed_species_habitat),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Total number of observed genera in all habitats across all sites and years:",
  nrow(observed_genus_habitat),
  "\n"
)

cat("Number of site × habitat × year combinations:", nrow(carabid_habitat_summary), "\n")
```

### Summary table
Let's make a summary table for my appendix, looking at carabids by habitat type and year
```{r}
# table summarizing carabid species abundance by habitat/ year
carabid_species_table <- carabid_long_habitat %>%
  group_by(carabid_species, habitat, year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_abundance = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  unite(habitat_year, habitat, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = habitat_year,
    values_from = total_abundance,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
  filter(Total > 0) %>%     # <-- keep only species with >0 counts
  arrange(desc(Total))

# Clean column names for Word (ie. remove the "_")
carabid_species_table <- carabid_species_table %>%
  mutate(
    carabid_species = gsub("_", " ", carabid_species)
  )


carabid_species_table

# save as table
write.csv(
  carabid_species_table,
  here::here("02_tables", "carabid_species_table.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```


### Sample Coverage and Hill Diversity
Let's calculate sample coverage and hill diversity by habitat using the iNEXT package to evaluate sample completeness among habitats and compare diversity patterns.

```{r}
# HILL DIVERSITY AND SAMPLE COVERAGE
# Summarize by habitat
carabid_by_habitat <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(species_columns), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Build iNEXT list: named abundance vectors (one per habitat)
carabid_list_habitat <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(carabid_by_habitat)), function(i) {
    v <- unlist(carabid_by_habitat[i, species_columns], use.names = TRUE)
    v[is.na(v)] <- 0
    v
  }),
  carabid_by_habitat$habitat
)

# Sample coverage + totals
carabid_sample_coverage <- DataInfo(carabid_list_habitat, datatype = "abundance")

carabid_sample_coverage

write.csv(
  carabid_sample_coverage,
  here::here("02_tables", "carabid_sample_coverage.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Hill numbers
carabid_hill <- iNEXT(carabid_list_habitat, q = c(0, 1, 2), datatype = "abundance")

# table for hill numbers
carabid_hill_diversity <- carabid_hill$AsyEst

carabid_hill_diversity

# save as csv
write.csv(
  carabid_hill_diversity,
  here::here("02_tables", "carabid_hill_diversity.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

VY sample completeness very high (~0.99), SNH slightly lower but still good (~0.96). 
Quite a few singletons (7 in SNH, 5 in VY), a couple doubles/ triples. 

Based on the output for hill diversity, higher observed and estimated species richness in VY, more uncertainty in SNH richness. 
Shannon/ simpson diversity higher in SNH but also higher uncertainty. Indicate SNH has a more even community, while VY are dominated by a few species


Let's make some plots to visualize diversity by both sample size and sample completeness

```{r}
# Coverage-based curves
carabid_sample_coverage <- ggiNEXT(carabid_hill, type = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = 10)
  )

carabid_sample_coverage


# Coverage-based Hill curves
carabid_hill_size <- ggiNEXT(carabid_hill, type = 1,
  facet.var="Order.q") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

carabid_hill_size


# Coverage-based Hill curves
carabid_hill_coverage <- ggiNEXT(
  carabid_hill,
  type = 3,
  facet.var = "Order.q"
) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors)

carabid_hill_coverage

```


### Data Exploration


#### Relative abundance plots
Let's visualize the carabid relative abundance (at the genus level since it's easier to read x axis)

```{r}
custom_colors <- c("VY"="#8E44AD","SNH"="#009E73")

# 1) Summarise total individuals per habitat x genus
carabid_species_habitat_rel <- carabid_long_genus_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, carabid_genus) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  mutate(rel_abund = n / sum(n)) %>%   # relative abundance within each habitat
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(n > 0)

# 2) Order species (overall abundance across all habitats)
species_order <- carabid_species_habitat_rel %>%
  group_by(carabid_genus) %>%
  summarise(total_n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(total_n) %>%
  pull(carabid_genus)

carabid_species_habitat_rel <- carabid_species_habitat_rel %>%
  mutate(carabid_genus = factor(carabid_genus, levels = species_order))

# 3) Bubble plot of relative abundance of each family by habitat type
carabid_genus_relative_abundance <- ggplot(carabid_species_habitat_rel,
       aes(x = carabid_genus, y = habitat,
           size = rel_abund, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, color = "black", alpha = 1) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Relative abundance") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Habitat") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,  face = "italic"),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none")


carabid_genus_relative_abundance


```
#### Abundance and richness by habitat
Now we'll look at the overall mean abundance and rarefied richness by habitat using boxplots

```{r}
# define custom colors
custom_colors <- c("VY"="#8E44AD","SNH"="#009E73")

# -----------------------------
# HABITAT ABUNDANCE, SPECIES RICHNESS, MEAN PER TRAP AND RAREFIED RICHNESS
# -----------------------------
# ALL HABITATS RICHNESS
sp_mat            <- as.matrix(dplyr::select(carabid_habitat_summary, all_of(species_columns)))
total_abundance   <- rowSums(sp_mat)
species_richness  <- rowSums(sp_mat > 0)

#   Use the minimum total individuals among groups with > min_m_individuals
min_m_individuals <- 20L
m_candidates      <- total_abundance[total_abundance > min_m_individuals]

rarefaction_m <- if (length(m_candidates)) min(m_candidates) else NA_integer_

# Rarefy (individual-based); NA if m not available
rarefied_richness <- if (is.na(rarefaction_m)) {
  rep(NA_real_, nrow(sp_mat))
} else {
  vegan::rarefy(sp_mat, sample = rarefaction_m)
}

# Assemble final summary table
carabid_habitat_data <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(site_ID, habitat, sample_period, year, trap_count) %>%
  mutate(
    total_abundance   = total_abundance,
    mean_per_trap     = ifelse(trap_count > 0, total_abundance / trap_count, NA_real_),
    species_richness  = species_richness,
    rarefied_richness = rarefied_richness,
    rarefaction_m     = rarefaction_m
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_ID, year, sample_period, habitat)

# calculate mean per trap by habitat
carabid_mean_by_habitat <- carabid_habitat_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(habitat) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_per_trap = mean(mean_per_trap, na.rm = TRUE),
    n             = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
carabid_mean_by_habitat


# plot mean abundance per trap by Habitat (VY/ SNH)
# lets use line plots to account for paired design (each site has a VY and SNH)
# we're using mean per plot instead of total abundance to account for traps lost in the field
carabid_abundance_line <- ggplot(
  carabid_habitat_data,
  aes(
    x = habitat,
    y = mean_per_trap,
    group = interaction(site_ID, year)
  )
) +
  # paired lines in grey
  geom_line(
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  # points coloured by habitat
  geom_point(
    aes(color = habitat),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Carabid abundance",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean abundance per trap"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) + theme(
  axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16)
)


carabid_abundance_line



# let's also try with boxplots
carabid_mean_abundance <- ggplot(carabid_habitat_data, aes(x = habitat, y = mean_per_trap, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.3, alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "black")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 20)) +
  labs(
    x = "Habitat type",
    y = "Abundance per trap"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
carabid_mean_abundance

# rarefied richness
carabid_rarefied_richness <- ggplot(carabid_habitat_data, aes(x = habitat, y = rarefied_richness, fill = habitat)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "black") +
  geom_text(
    data = habitat_n,
    aes(
      x = habitat,
      y = max(carabid_habitat_data$rarefied_richness, na.rm = TRUE) + 2,
      label = paste0("n = ", n)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Carabid Rarefied Richness by Habitat Type",
    x = "Habitat Type",
    y = "Carabid Rarefied Richness"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
    
carabid_rarefied_richness
```

Generally, much higher abundance in VY compared to SNH.

#### Carabid Traits by Habitat

```{r}

# upload the traits data (dispersal and status)
carabid_traits <- read.csv(here::here ("00_data", "carabid_traits.csv"))


# join to carabid habitat data (in long format)
carabid_long_traits_habitat <- carabid_long_habitat %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(carabid_traits, carabid_species, dispersal_power, status),
    by = "carabid_species"
  )


# summarize dispersal abundance by site_ID, habitat and year
dispersal_abundance_habitat <- carabid_long_traits_habitat %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, year, dispersal_power) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(count), .groups = "drop")

# summarize dispersal abundance by site_ID, habitat and year
status_abundance_habitat <- carabid_long_traits_habitat %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, year, status) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(count), .groups = "drop")

# pivot to wide format
dispersal_abundance_wide <- dispersal_abundance_habitat %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = dispersal_power,
    values_from = total_abundance,
    values_fill = 0  # fill missing combinations with 0
  )

# Make sure dispersal_abundance_habitat is prepared
status_abundance_plot <- status_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, status) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop")
status_abundance_plot <- status_abundance_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(status))

# Make sure dispersal_abundance_habitat is prepared
dispersal_abundance_plot <- dispersal_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, dispersal_power) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop")
dispersal_abundance_plot <- dispersal_abundance_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(dispersal_power))

status_colors <- c(
  "introduced" = "#E69F00",     # orange
  "native" = "#009E73"     # bluish green
)

# Custom colors (edit to match your desired palette)
dispersal_colors <- c(
  "brachypterous" = "#E69F00",     # orange
  "macropterous" = "#009E73",     # bluish green
  "polymorphic" = "#0072B2",     # sky blue
  "dimorphic" = "#7D3C98"     # blue
)

# Create the stacked bar chart for both dispersal and status
ggplot(dispersal_abundance_plot, aes(x = habitat, y = total_abundance, fill = dispersal_power)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dispersal_colors) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "No. carabids",
    fill = "dispersal",
    title = "dispersal composition by habitat type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Create the stacked bar chart
ggplot(status_abundance_plot, aes(x = habitat, y = total_abundance, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "No. carabids",
    fill = "Status",
    title = "Carabid status by habitat type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# Summarize total abundance by habitat and dispersal, then calculate proportion
dispersal_prop_habitat <- dispersal_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, dispersal_power) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_abundance / sum(total_abundance))

dispersal_prop_habitat <- dispersal_prop_habitat %>%
  filter(!is.na(dispersal_power))

# Summarize total abundance by habitat and dispersal, then calculate proportion
status_prop_habitat <- status_abundance_habitat %>%
  group_by(habitat, status) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(habitat) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_abundance / sum(total_abundance))


# set factor order for consistent pie layout
dispersal_prop_habitat$dispersal_power <- factor(dispersal_prop_habitat$dispersal_power)


# Plot pie chart by habitat using facet
carabid_dispersal_pie <- ggplot(dispersal_prop_habitat, aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = dispersal_power)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar("y") +
  facet_wrap(~habitat) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dispersal_colors) +
  labs(
    fill = "Wing type",
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "right", 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

carabid_dispersal_pie

# Plot pie chart by habitat using facet
carabid_status_pie <- ggplot(status_prop_habitat, aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar("y") +
  facet_wrap(~habitat) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors) +
  labs(
    fill = "Origin status",
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

carabid_status_pie

```

Higher proportion of native species in SNH compared to VY, and higher proportion of brachypterous and polymorphic wing types in SNH. But also much lower abundance overall in SNH, so actually similar number of individuals in each habitat.

## GLLVM's

### Spider GLLVM
This section uses generalized linear latent variable models (GLLVM) 


```{r}
# Pivot to long format to count presence
family_presence <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(family_columns)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "family", values_to = "count") %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(n_samples = sum(count > 0), .groups = "drop")

# Filter families with at least 5 non-zero entries
families_to_keep <- family_presence %>%
  filter(n_samples >= 5) %>%
  pull(family)
print(families_to_keep)

observed_families <- observed_families_habitat %>% dplyr::pull(spider_family)

# Response matrix (all family counts)
Y_spider <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(observed_families)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Filter Y to include only common species
Y_spider_rare_removed <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(families_to_keep)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Offset (log effort) and final response matrix 
effort_vec <- pmax(spider_habitat_summary$trap_count, 1L)
off_vec    <- log(effort_vec)


site_ID <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::pull(site_ID) %>%
  factor()

studyDesign <- data.frame(site_ID = factor(site_ID))


# Covariate C matrix (habitat and season only)
X_spider <- spider_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(habitat, year) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))


```


```{r}

# Fit GLLVM using factors habitat and year
# rare families (<5) removed
gllvm_spider_pois <- gllvm(
  y = Y_spider_rare_removed,
  X = X_spider,                        
  family = "poisson", 
  formula = ~ habitat + year,
  num.lv = 2,
  studyDesign = studyDesign,
  row.eff = ~(1 | site_ID),
  offset = off_vec,   
  method = "VA"
)

summary(gllvm_spider_pois)



```


#### Meeting model assumptions

Checking for collinearity
Model diagnostics and performance

```{r}
# biplot of the GLLVM 
plot(gllvm_spider_pois, biplot = TRUE, ind.spp = TRUE)
```

Residuals are fan shaped, indicating overdispersion. let's try a negative binomial distribution. 

```{r}
# Fit GLLVM using factors (without continuous covariates)
# rare families (<5) removed
gllvm_spider_nb <- gllvm(
  y = Y_spider_rare_removed,
  X = X_spider,                        
  family = "negative.binomial", 
  formula = ~ habitat + year,
  num.lv = 2,
  studyDesign = studyDesign,
  row.eff = ~(1 | site_ID),
  offset = off_vec,   
  method = "VA"
)

summary(gllvm_spider_nb)

```
```{r}
# biplot of the GLLVM 
plot(gllvm_spider_nb, biplot = TRUE, ind.spp = TRUE)
```

Residuals look better and AICc is smaller for NB model

#### Model outputs

Let's plot the gllvm model coefficients

```{r}
  cex.ylab = 0.7,
  mar = c(4, 10, 2, 1),
  xlim.list = list(
    c(-4, 4),   # habitat
    c(-4, 4)    # year
  )
)
```

### Spider Fourth Corner Model

First we'll prepare the traits dataset
```{r}
# FAMILY TRAITS
# Ensure the species names in traits match the columns in Y
spider_traits_rare_removed <- spider_traits %>% filter(spider_family %in% colnames(Y_spider_rare_removed))

# ensure it's a dataframe in the same order as Y
spider_traits_ordered <- spider_traits_rare_removed[match(colnames(Y_spider_rare_removed), spider_traits_rare_removed$spider_family), ]


# make spider_family the row names
rownames(spider_traits_ordered) <- spider_traits_ordered$spider_family

# keep only the guild code column
TR_spider <- spider_traits_ordered %>%
  dplyr::select(guild_code)

# Make sure it matches!
all(colnames(Y_spider_rare_removed) %in% rownames(TR_spider))
sum(colnames(Y_spider_rare_removed) %in% rownames(TR_spider))


# make sure reference levels make sense for model
X_spider$habitat <- relevel(factor(X_spider$habitat), ref = "SNH")

# set dispersal power reference level to macropterous
TR_spider$guild_code <- relevel(
  factor(TR_spider$guild_code),
  ref = "GRH"
)

```


```{r}
# run gllvm fourth corner model with spider traits
# still include site_ID as a row effect and offset
gllvm_spider_traits <- gllvm(
  y = Y_spider_rare_removed,
  X = as.data.frame(X_spider),
  TR = TR_spider,
  family = "negative.binomial",
  num.lv = 2,
  method = "VA",
  offset = off_vec,
  studyDesign = studyDesign,
  row.eff = ~(1 | site_ID),
  formula = y ~ habitat * (guild_code))

summary(gllvm_spider_traits)

```


#### Meeting model assumptions

Checking for collinearity
Model diagnostics and performance

Relative to SNH, VY support more SHW/ OTH 


### Carabid GLLVM

First we'll prepare the data and get it in the right format for GLLVM modelling

```{r}

# Offset (log effort) and final response matrix
effort_vec <- pmax(carabid_habitat_summary$trap_count, 1L)   # guard against 0
off_vec    <- log(effort_vec)

# --- site_ID: grouping factor for random site intercept -------------------
# one site label per sample row (should be length 90)
site_ID <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(site_ID) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))


Y_carabid <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(species_columns)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Covariate matrix (habitat and season only)
X_carabid <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(site_ID, habitat, year) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

# --- Identify rare species to exclude -------------------------------------
species_occurrence_summary <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(species_columns), ~ sum(. > 0))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "species", values_to = "n_samples")

# Threshold: must occur in at least 5 unique samples
species_to_keep <- species_occurrence_summary %>%
  filter(n_samples > 5) %>%
  pull(species)

# --- Filter Y to include only common species ------------------------------
Y_rare_carabid_removed <- carabid_habitat_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(species_to_keep)) %>%
  as.matrix()



```

Next we'll run the gllvm model (with poisson distribution to start)

```{r}
# Fit GLLVM using factors 
# rare species (<5) removed
# habitat as predictors (without continuous covariates)
# include 2 latent variables and offset
gllvm_carabid_pois <- gllvm(
  y = Y_rare_carabid_removed,
  X = X_carabid,
  family = "poisson",
  formula = ~ habitat + year,
  num.lv = 2,
  studyDesign = studyDesign,
  row.eff = ~(1 | site_ID),
  offset = off_vec,
  method = "VA"
)


summary(gllvm_carabid_pois)


```


#### Meeting model assumptions

```{r}
# plot the residuals
plot(gllvm_carabid_pois, biplot = TRUE, ind.spp = TRUE)

# no strong violation of homogeneity of variance.

```

Residuals seem okay for poisson model. 


#### Model outputs

Let's plot the model coefficients

```{r}

  gllvm_carabid_pois,
  cex.ylab = 0.7,
  mar = c(4, 10, 2, 1),
  xlim.list = list(
    c(-4, 4),   # habitat
    c(-4, 4)    # year
  )
)
```


and then clean up the plot axis and save

```{r}
  str_replace_all("_", " ") |>    
  str_to_sentence()
```

### Carabid Fourth Corner Model

First we'll prepare the trait data and make sure it lines up with the Y (response) dataframe.
Again, we'll only keep the carabid species with >5 individuals.
Let's also set the references as SNH, macropterous and native. 

```{r}
# SPECIES TRAITS
# Ensure the species names in traits match the columns in Y
carabid_traits_rare_removed <- carabid_traits %>% filter(carabid_species %in% colnames(Y_rare_carabid_removed))

# ensure it's a dataframe in the same order as Y
carabid_traits_ordered <- carabid_traits_rare_removed[match(colnames(Y_rare_carabid_removed), carabid_traits_rare_removed$carabid_species), ]

# make carabid_species the row names
rownames(carabid_traits_ordered) <- carabid_traits_ordered$carabid_species

# remove non-necessary columns
TR_carabid <- carabid_traits_ordered %>%
  dplyr::select(-carabid_species)     # remove non-trait columns

# Make sure it matches!
all(colnames(Y_rare_carabid_removed) %in% rownames(TR_carabid))
sum(colnames(Y_rare_carabid_removed) %in% rownames(TR_carabid))


# make sure reference levels make sense for model
X_carabid$habitat <- relevel(factor(X_carabid$habitat), ref = "SNH")

# set dispersal power reference level to macropterous
TR_carabid$dispersal_power <- relevel(
  factor(TR_carabid$dispersal_power),
  ref = "macropterous"
)

# set status to be introduced
TR_carabid$status <- relevel(
  factor(TR_carabid$status),
  ref = "native"
)


```


Now we'll run the gllvm fourth corner model with the traits included. 

```{r}
# run gllvm model
# Y is carabid matrix grouped by site/ habitat/ year
# X is predictor variables (habitat)
# TR is carabid traits
# offset for trap count, row effect for site ID
gllvm_carabid_traits <- gllvm(
  y = Y_rare_carabid_removed,
  X = as.data.frame(X_carabid),
  TR = TR_carabid,
  family = "negative.binomial",
  num.lv = 2,
  method = "VA",
  offset = off_vec,
  studyDesign = studyDesign,
  row.eff = ~(1 | site_ID),
  formula = y ~ habitat * (dispersal_power + status))

summary(gllvm_carabid_traits)

```

#### Meeting model assumptions
```{r}
# biplot of the GLLVM 
plot(gllvm_carabid_traits, biplot = TRUE, ind.spp = TRUE)
```
residuals look okay!

#### Model outputs

Plot and save fourth corner plot 

```{r}
coefplot(gllvm_carabid_traits)

a <- max( abs(carabid_fourth) )

# remove prefix (status/ dispersal power) for plotting
colnames(carabid_fourth) <- colnames(carabid_fourth) |>
  str_remove("^(status|dispersal_power)_?") |>  # remove either prefix
  str_replace("_", " / ")
colnames(carabid_fourth) <- colnames(carabid_fourth) |>
  str_to_sentence()


# add colors for habitats
colort <- colorRampPalette(c(
  custom_colors["SNH"],  # negative
  "white",
  custom_colors["VY"]    # positive
))


# plot fourth corner model using levelplot from lattice package

  xlab = "Habitat",
  ylab = "Species traits",
  col.regions = colort(100),
  at = seq(-a, a, length = 100),
  scales = list(x = list(draw = FALSE)),
  par.settings = list(
    axis.text = list(cex = 1.3),
    par.xlab.text = list(cex = 1.5),
    par.ylab.text = list(cex = 1.5),
    par.legend.text = list(cex = 1.3)
  )
)

carabid_4th_plot


# open device (save image using base R)

  filename = here::here("03_figures", "carabid_4th_plot.png"),

)
```
